sentences.text: Rinconsaurus was a titanosaur sauropod, a type of large herbivorous dinosaur, that possessed an unusually slender body compared to other members of its kind.

This animal is distinguished by unique tail vertebrae with bony processes, a feature that gave the specific name *caudamirus*, meaning "amazing tail," while the generic name refers to the discovery site Rincón de los Sauces.
Its mouth contained pencil-chisel-like teeth with sharply inclined wear facets, adapted for processing tough vegetation.
Fossils of Rinconsaurus were discovered in 1997 by Gabriel Benítez near Rincón de los Sauces in the Bajo de la Carpa Formation, Neuquén Province, Argentina.
The species Rinconsaurus caudamirus was formally described in 2003 based on three partial skeletons found at this location.
Rinconsaurus was an herbivore that fed on plants.
Fossilized dung from titanosaurids suggests Rinconsaurus ate a diet including palms and grasses, leading to speculation about co-evolution with grasses.
Rinconsaurus is classified as a titanosaurid sauropod.
In 2007, some researchers assigned Rinconsaurus to the tribe Aeolosaurini within the subfamily Saltasaurinae, and also to the clade Aeolosauridae.
In 2007, Calvo, González Riga, and Porfiri erected a clade named Rinconsauria for Rinconsaurus and Muyelensaurus, though this classification is not yet widely accepted.

Rinconsaurus lived approximately 83 million years ago during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, while other estimates place it between 85.7 and 83.6 million years ago during the Santonian stage.
